 National Poll: Rubio Leads 2028 GOP Nomination Contest, Ossoff Rises Among Democrats
 November 19th, 2026
 Home Polls National Poll: Rubio Leads 2028 GOP Nomination Contest, Ossoff Rises Among Democrats 
 Voters say cost of living should be top priority for Congress 
 The November 2026 Emerson College national poll finds President Trump with a 37% approval rating and 54% disapproval rating. Heading into a new Congress, voters were asked how much of a priority several issues should be for the delegation in 2027. Addressing the cost of living ranks the highest (57% top priority), followed by ending the war in Iran (49%), banning stock trading among members (49%), healthcare reform (45%), regulating the AI industry (37%), and investigating the Trump administration (28%).
 “Voters are most eager for Congress to address the cost of living: 71% of Democrats, 58% of independents, and 42% of Republicans think it should be the top priority for Congress in 2027,” Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling, said. “Half (50%) of Democrats think investigating the Trump administration should be the top priority for Congress, while 26% of independents say the same.”  
 Looking ahead to the 2028 Presidential Election, voters were offered first an open-ended response asking whom they would support for the Republican and Democratic nominations, then a closed-ended list among top candidates in Emerson polls. 
 In the open-ended Democratic Primary, Jon Ossoff (17%) and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (12%) top the list of candidates, followed by Gavin Newsom (8%), Pete Buttigieg (6%), Kamala Harris (6%), Andy Beshear (4%), and Mark Kelly (3%). 
 In the closed-ended question, 17% support Ossoff, 16% Kamala Harris, 15% AOC, 14% Pete Buttigieg, 11% Gavin Newsom, 7% Andy Beshear, 4% Mark Kelly, and 3% Josh Shapiro and JB Pritzker, respectively.
 In the open-ended Republican Primary, 36% named Marco Rubio, 20% JD Vance, 7% Ron DeSantis, 7% current President Donald Trump, and 7% Thomas Massie. 
 In the closed-ended question, 44% support Marco Rubio, 24% JD Vance, 9% Ron DeSantis, and 6% Donald Trump Jr. 
 When asked about the two major political parties, a majority have an unfavorable view of the Republican Party (56%), while 35% have a favorable view of it. The Democratic Party is also underwater by three points, 47% unfavorable to 44% favorable. Democrats’ favorable rating increased nine points in the past year. Republicans’ favorable rating decreased nine points, and their unfavorable rating increased 12 points to majority unfavorable at 56%.
 Methodology 
 The Emerson College Polling national survey was conducted November 14-16, 2026. The overall sample of U.S. voters, n=1,000, has a credibility interval, similar to a poll’s margin of error (MOE), of +/- 3 percent. The data sets were weighted by gender, education, race, age, party, and region based on U.S. Census parameters and voter file data. 
 It is important to remember that subsets based on demographics, such as gender, age, education, and race/ethnicity, carry with them higher credibility intervals, as the sample size is reduced. Survey results should be understood within the poll’s range of scores, and with a confidence interval of 95% a poll will fall outside the range of scores 1 in 20 times. 
 Data was collected by contacting a probability-based panel of voters provided by Consensus Strategies using MMS text-to-web, with additional panel interviews provided by PureSpectrum. All respondents were recruited using customized links that prevent responses from anyone outside of the poll’s sample frame. Panel responses were matched to the Aristotle voter file using respondents’ full name and ZIP code. The survey was administered using QuestionPro, and the survey was offered in English.
